To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed trajectory formulation improves driving performance and safety, (ii) conditional value at risk loss function helps to reduce the risk of rare events and (iii) the Gaussian mixture model improves the performance in the presence of multi-modal data.
We proposed a novel end-to-end architecture that is able to predict car actuatiors directly from raw sensory data.

(i) learning of a trajectory instead of the car actuators directly improves driving performance and interpretability, and (ii) using a conditional value at risk loss instead of a mean squared error loss improves driving performance in rare events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving E2E learning for autonomous vehicle systems.
improving the performance, safety, and interpretability of E2E autonomous driving systems.
improving the performance of end-to-end trained autonomous driving policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown the feasibility of the proposed approach and have demonstrated its effectiveness in the context of highway driving in TORCS.
the proposed architecture is able to improve the driving performance and reduce the number of collisions in the TORCS environment.
our proposed approach has shown to improve the performance of an end-to-end driving policy in the TORCS highway scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to show that a single model can learn to perform both lane keeping and lane changing in an end-to-end fashion.
we are able to achieve a good trade off between interpretability, safety, and learning efficiency, while maintaining end-to-end learning.
we have designed a driving policy which is safe, interpretable, and efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design an E2E driving policy which can learn from a limited number of samples, and can be made safe and explainable by enforcing a trajectory prior.
E2E learning is a promising direction for autonomous vehicle control.
E2E training can achieve good driving performance with safety enforcement and interpretability.
